content:
The Tampa Bay Rays refused to go quietly on Tuesday night, beating the Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings in Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg to keep their season alive.

Milwaukee still leads the best-of-seven series three games to one, but the Rays' extra-inning escape guarantees at least one more game in Florida.

The Brewers struck first in the fourth inning, added runs in the fifth and the twelfth, and looked headed for a sweep when Cooper Pratt's solo home run put Milwaukee ahead in the top of the 12th. Tampa Bay answered in the bottom of the inning: Jonny DeLuca tied the game with an RBI single, and Ben Williamson won it with a single to right field.

Ian Seymour was credited with the win for Tampa Bay, while Shane Drohan took the loss for Milwaukee. The Rays finished with nine hits to Milwaukee's eight.

The series opened in Milwaukee, where the Brewers won Game 1 by 3-2 and Game 2 by 5-4, then routed the Rays 10-1 in Game 3 on Monday night. Milwaukee, in its first World Series since 1982 and its first as a National League club, swept the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-0 in the National League Championship Series. Tampa Bay reached the World Series by beating the Cleveland Guardians 4-2 in the American League Championship Series.

Game 5 is Wednesday night, October 28, at Tropicana Field, with first pitch set for 8:00 p.m. ET on FOX. If necessary, the series returns to Milwaukee for Game 6 on Friday, October 30, and Game 7 on Saturday, October 31.

Sources: NBC Sports; USA Today; Smashology Media.

title: Rays Stay Alive With 4-3 Win in 12 Innings as Brewers Keep 3-1 World Series Lead
